A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAR research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The original metrics and case studies can be matched reliably across appendix renumbering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original GAR evaluations on MiniF2F-Test and ProofNet-Test, curriculum diagnostics and ablations in Tables 1–4, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds PutnamBench evaluation, statement-modification measurements and fuser ablations in Tables 5–7.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same statement fusion, autoformalization, adversarial GRPO objectives, filtering and modification penalties. The new fuser variants are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed GAR procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds evaluation on PutnamBench, covering 660 problems from an additional challenging formal-mathematics benchmark. MiniF2F-Test, ProofNet-Test and the Numina-Math/Lean-Workbook training sources are retained.

E2.justification: The prover baselines in Table 1 are unchanged. New Table 7 compares full GAR with Frozen Fuser and MagicCoder Fuser, the latter described as a MagicCoder-style single-problem enhancement strategy. Appendix C's discussion of STP and Goedel-Prover-V2 does not add evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a three-iteration frozen-fuser experiment on Goedel-Prover-V2-8B and a single-problem enhancement control. D.3 adds a MiniF2F-Test modification-rate assessment labeled pass@32. Previously reported training budgets, hyperparameters and verification rules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained difficulty, penalty and direct-RL studies, D.4 introduces targeted ablations testing whether the fuser must learn and whether two-problem fusion matters. D.3 additionally examines test-set statement modification. These substantially expand examination of GAR's central design choices; the original case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental results. The added tables continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 are unchanged. New results include PutnamBench scores of 22/660 for the base model versus 24/660 for GAR; modification rates of 6.96%/13.11% for base/GAR DeepSeek and 24.18%/27.05% for Goedel; and frozen-fuser/MagicCoder-fuser scores of 77.87%/75.41%, versus GAR's retained 80.33%. D.1 claims four additional PutnamBench solves, conflicting with Table 5's difference of two.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the mathematical metric definitions in v1 Appendix A/v2 Appendix B, and the displayed reasoning and Lean proof examples are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about adversarial co-training, implicit curriculum, efficiency and generality, including the headline MiniF2F and ProofNet gains. The appendix additions supply evidence for existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: D.2 replaces the efficiency discussion's local warning about prolonged RL degradation with an argument that different SFT/RL starting points strengthen the efficiency claim; scalability remains unresolved. D.3–D.4 add interpretations linking modification rates to self-correction and ablation outcomes to the necessity of fuser learning and fusion.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release and links a repository; v2's abstract newly states that training code is open-sourced there. However, future-release wording remains elsewhere in v2, making availability internally inconsistent. New acknowledgments also disclose Delta, DeltaAI and NAIRR computing resources.

R1.justification: New Appendix C explicitly distinguishes GAR from Goedel-Prover-V2's static RL statement set and STP's offline expert iteration. Added citations include iterative dataset synthesis, Magicoder, Lean4Physics, FANS and PhysProver. The main related-work sections and overall positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds ethics and reproducibility statements, acknowledgments and appendix subsections, with corresponding renumbering and localized discussion changes. The header changes to an ICLR 2026 publication statement. Most main-text exposition and both lengthy case studies remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–7 for PutnamBench, statement-modification rates and fuser ablations, with Table 7 placed beside case-study text. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–4 retain their basic displays; other differences are local repositioning and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The targeted fuser ablations provide a modest net gain in support for central design choices, and PutnamBench broadens validation. These benefits are tempered by D.1's inconsistent gain claim—four extra solves versus two in Table 5—and stronger efficiency conclusions despite different starting models. The revision adds useful evidence but does not resolve uncertainty reporting or fully justify its stronger interpretations.
